title: Berlin Rental Deposit - Quick Summary
items: **Three times the cold rent is the ceiling.** § 551 (1) BGB caps a deposit at three monthly rents **without** the service-charge advances. On the **7.71 euro per square metre** median in the Berliner Mietspiegel 2026, a 60 square metre flat means **462.60 euros** cold rent and a lawful cap of **1,387.80 euros**. You were also entitled to pay it in **three monthly instalments**, and any clause worse for you than the statute is void.

**Six months after the keys, damage claims die.** Under § 548 (1) BGB a landlord's claims for damage or alterations are time-barred **six months from the return of the flat**. After that date a scratched floor cannot be taken off your deposit at all, whatever the letter says.

**The service-charge reserve is the one lawful reason to wait longer.** The Federal Court of Justice (VIII ZR 71/05) lets a landlord hold back **an appropriate part** until the pending statement is due, and § 556 (3) BGB makes that statement due **twelve months after the accounting period ends**. On a calendar-year period, a flat handed back in March 2026 means a statement due by **31 December 2027**.

**Your own clock runs out too.** The claim prescribes **three years** after the end of the year it fell due, so a deposit payable in 2027 is chaseable until **31 December 2030**. Berlin deposits are lost to drift far more often than to theft.

**Never live off the deposit.** Skipping the last two months of rent is arrears, not a clever settlement, and two months of arrears is a ground for termination without notice under § 543 (2) no. 3 BGB.

**My move:** on handover day, sign a protocol with the meter readings, photograph every room, then put two calendar alarms in: six months out, and twelve months after that year's service-charge period ends. Write on the first alarm.
